skill.name: zarr-python
skill.description: Design and troubleshoot chunked Zarr arrays with compression, cloud storage, parallel I/O, and NumPy, Dask, or Xarray integration.
skill.summary: Plan efficient Zarr storage for large scientific arrays across local and cloud systems.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 90 static findings are contextual false positives. The detections are Markdown fences, fixed examples, documentation links, a Zarr group key listing, and chunking guidance; no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Use consolidated metadata to reduce latency: `zarr.consolidate_metadata(store)`
- Speeds up `tree()` operations and group traversal
- **Balance**: Larger chunks = fewer metadata operations; smaller chunks = better parallel access

content.value_statement: Large scientific arrays can overwhelm memory and make cloud storage inefficient. This skill guides chunking, compression, storage backends, parallel access, and ecosystem integrations with Zarr-Python.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to create, open, read, write, resize, and append Zarr arrays.
Recommends chunk sizes and shapes for sequential, row-wise, column-wise, random, and cloud access patterns.
Shows compression, sharding, consolidated metadata, and synchronization configurations.
Covers local, memory, ZIP, S3, and Google Cloud Storage backends.
Integrates Zarr with NumPy, Dask, Xarray, HDF5, and NetCDF workflows.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but does not benchmark workloads in the user environment.
Examples target Python 3.11 and Zarr 3.x, so installed APIs may require verification.
Cloud examples require user-provided credentials, permissions, buckets, and storage client configuration.
Optimal chunking and compression still require representative testing against memory, latency, throughput, and cost constraints.

use_cases.title: Scientific array storage
use_cases.description: Plan chunking and compression for large experimental, climate, or simulation arrays that exceed workstation memory.

use_cases.title: Cloud data pipelines
use_cases.description: Design S3 or GCS Zarr layouts with larger chunks, sharding, consolidated metadata, and parallel writes.

use_cases.title: Labeled parallel analytics
use_cases.description: Connect Zarr stores to Dask and Xarray for lazy computation, coordinate-based selection, and format conversion.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic array
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a beginner Zarr example for a {shape} {dtype} array stored at {path}, using chunks suitable for {access_pattern} access.

prompt_templates.title: Select chunks and compression
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend chunk sizes and compression for a {shape} {dtype} dataset with {access_pattern} reads and a {memory_limit} memory limit.
prompt_templates.scenario: Tune storage for a known workload.

prompt_templates.title: Design a cloud workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Zarr workflow that writes {dataset_type} data to {storage_backend} and reads it lazily with {Dask_or_Xarray}.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a scalable cloud data pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an advanced pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Zarr pipeline for memory, concurrency, metadata, and cloud request risks, then propose measured optimizations: {pipeline_description}.

output_examples.input: Plan storage for a 20,000 by 20,000 float32 matrix with mixed row and column reads.
output_examples.output: Use chunks near 512 by 512 as a starting point, then benchmark representative reads. Choose Zstandard for balanced compression and speed.

output_examples.input: Design lazy analysis for a climate dataset stored in S3.
output_examples.output: Store the dataset with cloud-sized chunks and consolidated metadata. Open it through Xarray for labels and Dask for lazy computation.

output_examples.input: Convert a large HDF5 dataset to Zarr without loading it entirely into memory.
output_examples.output: Read the HDF5 dataset in bounded slices and write matching Zarr chunks. Validate shape, dtype, metadata, and representative values before replacement.

best_practices: Choose chunk shapes from measured access patterns, then benchmark representative reads and writes.
Keep chunks and shards within memory limits, especially during compression and parallel writes.
Consolidate metadata for read-heavy cloud stores, then refresh it after structural updates.
anti_patterns: Avoid loading complete arrays with full slices when datasets can exceed available memory.
Do not let concurrent workers write overlapping chunks without synchronization or partitioning.
Do not select compression levels or cloud chunk sizes without measuring latency, throughput, and cost.

faq.question: Which Python and Zarr versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: The guidance targets Python 3.11 or later and Zarr-Python 3.x. Verify APIs against the installed version.

faq.question: Does the skill configure cloud credentials?
faq.answer: No. Cloud examples rely on credentials and permissions already configured through the selected storage client.

faq.question: Can it choose an optimal chunk size automatically?
faq.answer: It recommends starting points from array shape, dtype, access patterns, and storage backend. Benchmarking is still required.

faq.question: Does it support Zarr version 2 stores?
faq.answer: The reference notes Zarr v2 and v3 compatibility, but examples emphasize current Zarr-Python interfaces.

faq.question: Does the skill execute data operations?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example workflows for an agent to adapt within the user-approved environment.

faq.question: Can it integrate Zarr with Dask and Xarray?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers lazy Dask reads and writes, Xarray datasets, labeled selection, and cloud-backed workflows.
